roads.name: Highway 17
words: Properly twisty: 18 curves in 2.5 miles, about 7 a mile.
The curves flow straight into one another.
From 9,408 to 9,826 ft, with 520 ft of up and down along the way.
roads.ratingNote: A full bar is top marks for that part; the percentages are each part's share of the rating. Curves, length and up and down are ranked against every road in the library. The rest are scored on the road itself: how few side roads join it, whether the curves or the limit set the pace, and how little is built up along it. At the 55 mph limit its corners still ask for about 0.83 g, so the curves, not the limit, set the pace.

roads.name: Pinos Creek Road
words: An easygoing road: 7 curves in 4.0 miles, with room to breathe between them.
From 7,906 to 8,177 ft, with 371 ft of up and down along the way.
roads.ratingNote: A full bar is top marks for that part; the percentages are each part's share of the rating. Curves, length and up and down are ranked against every sweeper in the library. The rest are scored on the road itself: how few side roads join it, whether the curves or the limit set the pace, and how little is built up along it. At the 55 mph limit its corners still ask for about 0.81 g, so the curves, not the limit, set the pace. Most of it has no posted limit on the map, so this assumes 55 mph.

roads.name: Highway 160
words: Sweeping and steady: 20 curves in 4.1 miles.
The 1.9 miles at the north end are tamer.
The curves flow straight into one another.
From 8,118 to 9,560 ft, with 1,494 ft of up and down along the way.
